s.b: Press play for a two-minute tour of what the plugin does, or read the overview below. TeamzLab FedEx Shipping is a WooCommerce plugin for stores that ship with FedEx. In plain words, it: shows live FedEx shipping prices while your customer checks out, creates the FedEx label for you after a purchase, tracks shipments and lets customers follow their parcel on your site, supports FedEx freight (LTL) shipments, and gives your customers a self-service return portal. It runs on your own FedEx account. You enter your FedEx API credentials once; after that, the plugin talks to FedEx for you. Version 1.2.3 works with WordPress 6.x, WooCommerce up to 11.2, and PHP 7.4 or newer. See Compatibility .

Your store does not talk to FedEx directly — it asks FedEx’s interface for software (called an API, see the glossary ) for prices, and sends it label requests. To allow that, FedEx needs to know which account is asking. This page walks you through getting a set of test keys from FedEx, entering them in the plugin, and proving they work. Test keys are free and safe: labels created with them never move real packages and never cost money. You set everything up first and switch to real keys only when you are ready to go live.

t: Quick start: your first test label

s.h: Quick start: your first test label
s.b: Prefer to watch first? The video runs the whole quick start end to end; the written steps below are the same path at your own pace. This page is the shortest path from zero to seeing the plugin work. Everything stays in FedEx’s sandbox (the test environment): no real packages move and FedEx does not charge you. Allow about 15 minutes once you have your FedEx API keys. Sandbox labels are tests. They never move a real package, and nothing on this page creates real charges. You switch to production only when you deliberately go live — see Going live . 1 Install and activate the plugin Install the plugin — search for Teamzlab Fedex — on the WordPress Plugins screen and click Activate . The full walkthrough, including manual ZIP upload, is on Installation . After activation, a new FedEx Shipping menu appears in your WordPress admin. 2 Get sandbox API keys from FedEx The detailed version is on Connecting FedEx credentials . In short: Sign in at the FedEx Developer Portal with your FedEx account. Create a new API project and enable at least Rates & Transit Times , Ship , and Address Validation . FedEx updates its portal often — follow the current Create Project flow rather than any exact clicks quoted elsewhere. Choose the sandbox (test) environment for the project. Copy the API key (the Client ID) and the Secret key (the Client Secret). 3 Enter the keys in the plugin Go to WordPress Admin → FedEx Shipping → Settings . On the Authorization tab, enter your keys in Client ID and Client Secret . Open the Account tab and select Sandbox in Environment (the last field on that tab). Click Save Changes . WordPress reloads and shows a “Settings saved.” confirmation, and a Sandbox badge appears at the top of the Settings page. The Authorization tab, where the Client ID and Client Secret go. 4 Add the Fedex Shipping method to a shipping zone Go to WordPress Admin → WooCommerce → Settings → Shipping . Open the zone that covers the address you will test with. If you have no zone yet, click Add zone and add one that covers your country. Click Add shipping method , select Fedex Shipping , click Continue , then Save zone and method . The method’s window has only an on/off checkbox and a title — there is nothing FedEx-specific to configure per zone; the services and prices shown at checkout come straight from FedEx. The full walkthrough is on Add FedEx to a shipping zone . 5 Place a test order On your store, add any product to the cart and go to checkout. Enter a delivery address inside the shipping zone you used. Select one of the FedEx services offered and place the order. FedEx prices appear under the shipping options within a few seconds. The plugin is in instant mode by default, so the label is created automatically the moment the order is placed. Checkout prices can be cached for up to 10 minutes. If you just changed your settings and want fresh prices immediately, save the Settings page once — saving forces one fresh quote. 6 See the result Go to WordPress Admin

s.b: A quick video orientation comes first; the full A-to-Z list is in the table below. These are the words you will meet in this documentation and in your FedEx developer account. Terms are in alphabetical order. Where a deeper guide exists, the term links to it. Term Plain-English definition Advanced mode A shipping mode where checkout creates a draft shipment only; you review the packages and confirm it in the admin before any label is bought. See Open Ship . AIV The abbreviation the plugin uses for the tracking webhook feed — you will see it in the Tracking Webhooks (AIV) section on the Tracking tab. See Tracking webhooks . API key / Client ID The public half of the credential pair that identifies your store to FedEx. You paste it into Settings → Authorization. See Credentials . Commercial invoice The customs form that lists what an international package contains and what it is worth. The plugin fills it in automatically from the order. Customs The check every international shipment goes through at the border, where paperwork is inspected and duties and taxes are decided. Declared value The monetary value attached to a package or commodity line. The plugin takes it from the product prices on the order; in Advanced mode you can set it per package. Daily quota The number of FedEx checkouts your plan allows per day: 10 on Free, 100 on Premium, unlimited on Golden. It resets itself at midnight, your store’s local time. Developer portal FedEx’s website at developer.fedex.com where you create projects and get your API keys. Dimensional weight A pricing rule that charges a big-but-light package by its size instead of its weight. FedEx decides it; the plugin also ships a calculator your customers can use. Electronic Trade Documents (ETD) Sending customs paperwork to FedEx digitally instead of printing it and attaching it to the box. See International and ETD . FedEx API The connection the plugin uses to talk to FedEx: it sends addresses and package details, and FedEx sends back prices, labels, and tracking updates. Freight (LTL) “Less-Than-Truckload” shipping for pallets that are too big for normal parcels. FedEx LTL Freight services can appear at checkout when FedEx quotes them for a heavy cart. HPOS High-Performance Order Storage — WooCommerce’s modern way of saving orders in its own database tables. The plugin works with it. HS code An international product-classification code (Harmonized System) used on customs paperwork. The plugin reads it from a hidden product field or suggests it from the product name. See International ETD . Instant mode The default shipping mode: a label is bought automatically the moment the customer checks out. See Instant labels . Label rotation A setting on the Labeling tab that turns the printed label sideways or upside down so it fits your printer or label stock. See Labeling . Liftgate A lift on the delivery truck that lowers heavy freight to the ground when there is no loading dock. The plugin recognizes the option for f

A short video walkthrough is below; after it, every field on this tab is explained in order. WordPress Admin → FedEx Shipping → Settings , then the Account tab. This tab identifies who ships : the FedEx account that gets billed, the contact printed on labels, and the address every parcel starts from. It also holds the Environment switch between sandbox and production. Labels ship from this address. Return labels use the same address as the recipient — it is where your customers send returns to. The street lines of the address are entered separately on the Labeling tab . The FedEx Shipping settings page, Account tab. One Save Changes button at the bottom of the page saves all five tabs together — you cannot save a single tab on its own. Saving also refreshes stored shipping prices, so the next quote is fresh. All settings are saved with your WordPress site; there are no files or databases for you to touch.

Watch the two-minute setup video, or use the field-by-field reference below. WordPress Admin → FedEx Shipping → Settings , then the Authorization tab. The Authorization tab holds the two credentials that switch the plugin on. Every feature except tracking uses them: checkout rates, label creation, address validation, pickups, store locations, return labels, and trade documents. Tracking uses its own separate pair on the Tracking tab . The FedEx Shipping settings page, Authorization tab. The quota panel appears further down the page, below the Save bar.

t: Shipping one order in several packages

s.h: Shipping one order in several packages
s.b: The video shows a multi-box order in both modes; the written explanation follows. Sometimes one order cannot travel in one box: the items do not fit a single carton, or the customer bought several bulky products. FedEx handles this as one shipment made of several packages — one shipment, many boxes, many labels. The FedEx Shipping plugin supports this in both shipping modes. The difference between them is simply who decides what goes in each box.

t: Advanced mode (Open Ship): confirm shipments yourself

s.h: Advanced mode (Open Ship): confirm shipments yourself
s.b: Watch a draft become a confirmed shipment in the video, then read the full lifecycle below. Advanced mode changes when the label is bought . Your customer checks out exactly as before — same FedEx prices, same order confirmation — but the plugin does not buy a label at checkout. Instead, the order gets a FedEx Open Ship session : a working shipment that FedEx keeps open for you. You review the packages on the order screen and click one button to create the labels. A “draft session” is simply an unconfirmed shipment. FedEx knows the packages are coming, but nothing is paid for and no label exists until you confirm.
